The season kicked off on 28 March 2009 and ended on 25 October 2009. Winners and runners-up were promoted to [[Chinese Super League]] [[2010 Chinese Super League|next season]] and the last placed team was relegated to [[China League Two|League Two]]. League One would be expanded to 14 teams the season after. [[Zhu Zhengrong]] of [[Shanghai Port F.C.|Shanghai East Asia]] scored the first hat-trick of the season against [[Sichuan F.C.|Sichuan]] at [[Shanghai Stadium]] on 28 August 2009. [[Léo Gamalho]] of [[Shenyang Dongjin F.C.|Shenyang Dongjin]] scored the second hat-trick of the season against [[Shanghai Shenxin F.C.|Nanchang Bayi Hengyuan]] at [[Shenyang Olympic Stadium]] on 10 October 2009. [[Martín García (footballer, born 1981)|Martin García]] of Nanchang Bayi Hengyuan scored the third hat-trick of the season against [[Nanjing Yoyo F.C.|Nanjing Yoyo]] at [[Bayi Stadium]] on 25 October 2009. ==Promotion and relegation== After [[2008 in Chinese football|2008 season]], [[Jiangsu F.C.|Jiangsu Sainty]] and [[Chongqing Liangjiang Athletic F.C.|Chongqing Lifan]] were promoted to [[2009 Chinese Super League]] and [[Shaoxing Keqiao Yuejia F.C.|Yantai Yiteng]] were relegated to [[2009 China League Two]]. They were replaced by [[Shaanxi Wuzhou F.C.|Guangdong Sunray Cave]] and [[Shenyang Dongjin F.C.|Shenyang Dongjin]] which were promoted from [[2008 China League Two]] and [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning
